HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 3, 2025
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810
  HOUSING AUTHORITY, 4:00 PM

Julie Lie, Chair  Doug Killion, Member
Sarah Bedy, Member  Leanna Noble, Member
Pam Chotiswatdi, Member  Angela Russell, Member
Laurence Hilliard, Member  Patricia Scott, Member
James Howat, Member  Stephen Wood, Member

  FINISHED AGENDA & DRAFT MINUTES

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Julie Lie called the meeting to order at 4:03pm.

ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present: Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Killion, Noble, Russell, Scott, Wood, Lie

  Commissioners Absent: Hilliard

Also present: Paul Duncan, Homeless Services Bureau Manager, Jennifer Santana, Community
Program Specialist.

Roll call was take by Clerk Jennifer Santana.
  • For the record commissioner absent is unexcused.

REGULAR AGENDA

1.  25-57042  Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Homeless Services Advisory
  Committee meeting of Wednesday, October 1, 2025.

  A motion was made by Member Howat, seconded by Member Killion, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  9  Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Killion, Noble, Russell, Scott, Wood, Lie
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Hilliard

2.  25-57043  Recommendation to receive and file updates from the Mayor’s Fund and Policy
  Subcommittee and the Continuum of Care (CoC) Homeless Services Advisory
  Committee (HSAC) representative.

  Page 1 of 6
   HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 3, 2025
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810
  HOUSING AUTHORITY, 4:00 PM

  Mayor’s Fund Subcommittee
  • Member Jim Howat provided updates regarding the utility bill inserts, staff
  will follow up on time frame.
  • Member Leanna Noble would like the subcommittee establish an annual
  fundraising goal.
  Policy Subcommittee
  • Member Sarah Bedy provided updates, the subcommittee reviewed the
  annual policy recommendations. Sarah has encouraged members to meet
  with council members and discuss these recommendations.
  • The subcommittee is excited to hear more about the portable shower that the
  city has purchased. They will continue to discuss city owned vacant spaces
  that can be used for a pilot program.
  • Member Pat Sott would like to encourage this subcommittee to look into
  alternative projects, raised a few questions. Staff encouraged members to
  establish an Ad Hoc committee to discuss these topics.
  CoC Updates
  • Member Pat Scott provided an update, the board met last month to discuss
  the NOFO, HUD is shifting funding from permanent housing to transitional
  housing. The board will meet again on December 18th to vote on these
  items.
  • Member Leanna Noble encouraged staff to be creative in response to the
  NOFO, , adding that she would like to see the City take a stance consistent
  with the strong position it has taken on immigration laws.
  Public comment
  • A member of the public requested more information regarding the application
  process and approval for the Mayor’s Fund applications that are submitted.
  • A member of the public raised concerns regarding funding sources.

  A motion was made by Member Killion, seconded by Member Chotiswatdi, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  9  Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Killion, Noble, Russell, Scott, Wood, Lie
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Hilliard

3.  25-57044  Recommendation to review and vote on the Mayor’s Fund Subcommittee grant
  application submitted by Long Beach Community Table for funding in the amount
  of $31,507.46.

  Page 2 of 6
   HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 3, 2025
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810
  HOUSING AUTHORITY, 4:00 PM

  • Member Jim Howat advised the committee that the Mayor’s Fund
  subcommittee was not able to reach a decision on the Long Beach
  Community Table (LBCT) application. Staff and subcommittee members
  agree that the current application submitted does not meet the intent of the
  Mayor’s fund. The fund is not intended to cover operational cost but rather
  meet gap needs.
  • Director Kristen Cox from LBCT provided an overview of the program and
  the clients they serve. Discussed the need for the money to cover forklift
  breakdown.
  • The committee moved to receive and file the application as a discussion,
  LBCT is encouraged to reapply with a revised budget and request.

  A motion was made by Member Bedy, seconded by Member Killion, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  9  Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Killion, Noble, Russell, Scott, Wood, Lie
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Hilliard

4.  25-57048  Recommendation to receive and file a discussion on the City-owned shelter beds
  and temporary shelter report from the Health Department.

  A motion was made by Member Howat, seconded by Member Killion, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  9  Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Killion, Noble, Russell, Scott, Wood, Lie
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Hilliard

  • Bureau Manager Paul Duncan provided an update, Long Beach has multiple
  Interim Housing programs, these projects provide a place to stay but are not
  intended to be permanent housing. Interim housing types include transitional
  housing, congregate shelter, non-congregate shelter, and safe haven
  spaces.
  • Shelter beds within HUD include year-round shelter, seasonal beds and flex
  beds. Fluctuations of shelters can include shelters that have been converted
  into permanent housing, master leasing of motels/hotels became common
  after COVID.
  • PHK has opened as of December 1, 2025, 28 people have been moved in

  Page 3 of 6
   HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 3, 2025
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810

  since Monday.
  • The housing inventory for the past 5 yrs was reviewed, this inventory is given
  to HUD around the time that the Point In-Time Count is conducted.
  • Members of the committee have questions regarding the table presented
  and fluctuations. Members also raise questions regarding
  emergency vouchers, staff advise that there will be no vouchers moving
  forward.
  • Members of the committee and staff discuss alternatives following the loss of
  future funding.
  • A member of the public commented on the presentation printout.
  • A member of the public requested further explanation on the data table
  presented.

5.  25-57049  Recommendation to receive and file a presentation on the 2025 Built for Zero
  Conference from the Health Department.

  A Laid Over was made by Member Howat, seconded by Member Killion, Laid
  Over. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  9  Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Killion, Noble, Russell, Scott, Wood, Lie
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Hilliard

  • This agenda item was laid over to the meeting on February 4, 2026.

6.  25-57047  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Services Bureau Quarterly
  Operations Data Report and Staff Operations and Updates Report from the Health
  Department.

  A motion was made by Member Howat, seconded by Member Chotiswatdi, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  9  Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Killion, Noble, Russell, Scott, Wood, Lie
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Hilliard

  • Bureau Manager Paul Duncan provided an update, the department of Health
  and Human Services is going through a loss of multiple funding

  Page 4 of 6
   HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 3, 2025
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810
  HOUSING AUTHORITY, 4:00 PM

  sources/grants.
  • The bureau is working on assessing priorities and working to ensure stability
  in the future.
  • The NOFO was released on November 13, 2025, there are significant shifts
  in HUD policies and priorities in comparison to previous NOFOs.
  • On November 20, 2025 LA County provided an overview of Measure A
  recommendations for the next fiscal year. There is a projected $300 million
  deficit. The recommendation would be an $8.2 million reduction within the
  Long Beach CoC Budget.
  • Project Home key at 5950 former Luxury Inn had there ribbon cutting on
  Monday December 1, 2025.
  • Members of the committee discussed the possibility of assigning two people
  per room so they can support one another in light of funding cuts.
  • The Data report item was laid over to the meeting on February 4, 2026.

7.  25-57050  Recommendation to approve future agenda items.

  • Items tables will be discussed at the next meeting, the committee would also
  like a presentation on the Shower program.

  A motion was made by Member Howat, seconded by Member Wood, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  9  Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Howat, Killion, Noble, Russell, Scott, Wood, Lie
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Hilliard

VICE CHAIR ELECTION

PUBLIC COMMENT

  • No public comment.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

  • No announcements.

ADJOURNMENT
